suchun--ulbul.scene: INTRODUCING KING SUCHUN, who accepted the cup and had already counted the screens. Night in the inner hall at Gungnae. Low three-quarter from beside the banquet table: he sits in deep red court silk and the gold Goguryeo openwork crown, short black beard, heavy brows, one hand on the cup, looking past the camera at the brother who poured, quiet, not smiling: "You called, I came." A floor lamp at the table edge rakes him from the side in hard #8b1e2d. Behind him, painted loosely: dark timber, a painted screen about to drop, lamp smoke, one flame as bokeh. At the frame edge only an out-of-focus scarlet sleeve of the host. NEVER a smile. NEVER jougwan.

bongsang-prince--ulbul.scene: INTRODUCING PRINCE SABURU, the boy behind the pillar. Night in the same hall, two heads already on the floor. Low three-quarter from the packed earth beside a timber pillar: a FOURTEEN-YEAR-OLD Korean boy, NO beard, NO crown, black hair in a topknot, thin red po, hiding, looking past the camera at the floor with the same heavy brow as the later king, mouth shut, learning: he does not make a sound. Face STRUCTURE from the attached sheet, youthened, never the bearded crowned portrait. A lamp through the screens rakes one cheek in #6e2a2a. Behind him, painted loosely: the pillar, dark plaster, a smear of red on the floor dissolving. At the frame edge only an out-of-focus gold crown of the sitting uncle. NEVER a grown beard. NEVER a crown on this boy.

bongsang--ulbul.scene: INTRODUCING KING BONGSANG, who remembers who poured and will not be poured on. Night in the Gungnae hall, the crown already on him. Low three-quarter from below the dais: he sits in burgundy-red court silk and the gold openwork crown, short black beard, offended precise mouth, looking DOWN past the camera at a man who has just spoken too long: "Stop." A bronze floor lamp lights him from below in hard #6e2a2a. Behind him, painted loosely: red pillars, a dark screen, lamp smoke, one flame as bokeh. At the frame edge only an out-of-focus court sleeve of the prime minister. NEVER kind. NEVER a boy.

eummo--ulbul.scene: INTRODUCING UMMO, the stall boss. Rest is theft. Talk is theft. Day at the salt trestle under a far red munru. Low three-quarter from the packed earth beside a sack: he is mid-tie, older round Korean face, WHITE hair in a topknot, thin white moustache and goatee, brick-red po with white sleeves and a dotted hem, navy-black sash, stocky, not looking at the boy, mouth flat: "Sack. Tie it. Mouth shut." A hard cool market-sun rakes him from the side in #6b5a48. Behind him, painted loosely: pale paper sky, timber trestle, white hemp extras dissolving, the fortress a tiny red stamp. At the frame edge only an out-of-focus satgat brim of the hired boy. NEVER a young face. NEVER court silk.

jaemo--ulbul.scene: INTRODUCING JAEMO, who talks first and counts later, except when the young one is watching. Day at the same stall. Low three-quarter from beside the measure: he leans on the trestle, square Korean face, NO beard, satgat with a long red tail-cord, white hemp po, rust-red vest, black sash, white salt rope over the shoulder, mouth already open, protective: "Ours. He doesn’t talk much." A hard market-sun rakes his cheek in #c4a574. Behind him, painted loosely: pale paper sky, aisles of white hemp, a persimmon stall dissolving. At the frame edge only an out-of-focus white satgat of the silent partner. NEVER jougwan. NEVER court silk.

micheon-exile--ulbul.scene: INTRODUCING ULBUL, who has not used his name since the night his father told him to stop. Day at the stall under the fortress. Low three-quarter from the packed earth: he stands tying a measure, young dry Korean face, long black braid, straw satgat with a red cloth tail, white hemp po, brown inner, red sash, salt sack on the back, the sly look tired, looking UP past the camera at a red munru off-frame: "……Just a salt merchant." A hard cool sun rakes the satgat brim and the red sash in #C30000. Behind him, painted loosely: pale paper sky, timber trestle, the fortress a small red stamp on the ridge. At the frame edge only an out-of-focus rust vest of the mouthy partner. NEVER a crown. NEVER king silk. NEVER jougwan.

changjori--ulbul.scene: INTRODUCING CHANGJORI, who puts his knees in the mud before he puts a reed in his hat. Day on the Biryu bank. Low three-quarter from the wet packed earth: he is coming down the bank, lean Korean face, short goatee, long black hair, small black cap with TWO thin red antenna-feathers, red po over white inner, black shoulder boards, court silk already wrecked with mud, one knee about to hit, frightened of his own courage, mouth open: "The mud’s fine." A hard paper-white sky, the figure the dark inked thing. #8a7048 in the ruined silk. Behind him, painted loosely: the dark slope, empty white sky, a boat as a tiny stroke on the water. At the frame edge only an out-of-focus satgat of the salt seller. NEVER a gold crown. NEVER a clasped-hands portrait stance.

jumong-exile--ulbul.scene: INTRODUCING JUMONG, the first king, the first time this book lets you see the face. Night in Jumong Cavern, spirit-steam in the dark. Low three-quarter from the packed earth: he sits already on a rock in the steam, lean archer, knotted RED headband with long tails, RED po over charcoal inner, bow across his back, CLEAN-SHAVEN (ignore the portrait moustache), SERIOUS — the grin is gone, not a grim founder statue, looking at the kneeling salt seller off-frame: "Hey. You. Salt." NO gold crown. A shaft of leaf-light from the cave mouth rakes his red silk in #e8563f. Behind him, painted loosely: the wide stone mouth, tree trunks, steam and red-ember motes, two paler ancestor-shapes dissolving. At the frame edge only an out-of-focus satgat brim. NEVER facial hair. NEVER a king crown. NEVER a grin.

dolgo--ulbul.scene: INTRODUCING PRINCE DOLGO, the brother people smiled for. Night in a palace doorway, the cup already in his other hand. Low three-quarter from inside the room: he stands on the threshold, long black hair, short neat beard, warm almost-smiling mouth that is not smiling now, tall black official cap, red Goguryeo court robe with grey shoulder boards, looking at his son off-frame, one hand pushing, the other hiding the cup: "Go. Now. The back door." A corridor lamp rakes his face from the side in #9a5348. Behind him, painted loosely: the dark timber leaf, a cup on the threshold, lamp smoke. At the frame edge only an out-of-focus boy’s shoulder already turning. NEVER a crown. NEVER a cruel face.
